title: Unconventional Pressure Evolution of Spin-Density-Wave State in La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$
authors: Xiaoxiang Zhou, Shiyu Xie, Liangxin Qiao, Hengyuan Zhang, Jun Shu, Rui Liu, Mengwu Huo, Deyuan Hu, Hengjie Liu, Chuansheng Hu, Yilin Wang, Ge He, Zeming Qi, Meng Wang, Dong-Lai Feng, Zengyi Du
abstract: The discovery of pressure-induced high temperature superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$ has raised the question of how its spin-density-wave (SDW) state evolves toward the superconducting regime. Here, we report a systematic electronic Raman study of La$_{3}$Ni$_{2}$O$_{7}$ single crystals under hydrostatic pressures up to 16.51 GPa. Both the SDW gap energy and the transition temperature $T_{\mathrm{SDW}}$ show an overall increase with pressure, while the dimensionless coupling ratio 2$Δ_{\text{SDW}}/(k_{\text{B}}T_{\text{SDW}})$ remains constant around $\sim7.5$, indicating a robust strong-coupling character of SDW state. At the same time, the Raman SDW peak broadens as pressure is applied, indicating a gradual weakening of long-range SDW order. These results reveal an unusual pressure evolution in which the SDW energy scale is enhanced while the SDW state becomes progressively less coherent, providing spectroscopic constraints on the magnetic correlations relevant to superconductivity in bilayer nickelates.
summary: This work uses high-pressure electronic Raman spectroscopy to track the evolution of the SDW state in $	ext{La}_3	ext{Ni}_2	ext{O}_7$. It reveals that while the SDW energy scale increases with pressure, the coherence of the SDW state simultaneously decreases. This provides key insights into the magnetic correlations relevant to the high-temperature superconductivity emerging in this nickelate system.
main_problem: The study investigates how the Spin-Density-Wave (SDW) state in the bilayer nickelate $	ext{La}_3	ext{Ni}_2	ext{O}_7$ evolves as hydrostatic pressure is applied toward the superconducting regime.
main_result: The SDW gap energy and transition temperature both increase with pressure, indicating an enhanced energy scale, while the peak broadens, suggesting a weakening of long-range SDW order.
method: Systematic electronic Raman spectroscopy was performed on single crystals under hydrostatic pressures up to 16.51 GPa.
model_or_system: The physical system is the bilayer nickelate $	ext{La}_3	ext{Ni}_2	ext{O}_7$, whose low-energy physics is modeled by a bilayer $t-J$ model. The research focuses on the competition and evolution between the SDW state and superconductivity.
key_observables: SDW gap energy ($\Delta_{	ext{SDW}}$), SDW transition temperature ($T_{	ext{SDW}}$), dimensionless coupling ratio ($2\Delta_{	ext{SDW}}/(k_B T_{	ext{SDW}})$), and Raman peak linewidth ($\Gamma_{	ext{SDW}}$).
important_parameters: Hydrostatic pressure (up to 16.51 GPa); the strong-coupling ratio ($\sim 7.5$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed Raman response is dominated by the SDW electronic excitation continuum, which is fitted using a Lorentzian function.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the pressure-temperature phase diagram, confirming $T_{	ext{SDW}}$ increases with pressure. Figure 2 details the pressure-dependent $	ext{B}_{1g}$-symmetric Raman response, showing both energy shift and broadening.
paper_structure: The paper systematically measures the electronic Raman response across a wide pressure range, analyzing the pressure dependence of the SDW gap, transition temperature, and coherence, and interpreting these trends in the context of the SDW-superconductivity interplay.
why_interesting: The observation of a robust strong-coupling ratio alongside a weakening of long-range order provides crucial spectroscopic constraints on the magnetic correlations that are believed to mediate superconductivity in nickelates.
